title: Performance Margin Playbook — Alleyway Notes
content:
Purpose:

This is a lightweight, intentionally messy playbook for sales and growth to run short field experiments and tighter claims around ‘how we are faster and cheaper’. Focus is on defensible, repeatable lines and the minimal evidence set needed to back them in customer conversations. Not a polished pitch — notes, scripts, counterpoints, and test ideas.

High-level claim framework (one-liners we can stand behind if we have the data):
- Headline claim: ‘Design throughput and routing so you get consistent sub-100ms p95 generation at low cost for common prompt lengths.’ (requires per-model p95 evidence and cost compare)
- Secondary: ‘For short-turn chat workloads (<=256 tokens) customers see 2–4x cost-per-response improvement vs. single-instance baseline through batching + prefix cache.’
- Fallback safety claim: ‘If a pinned model is overloaded, automated routing to compatible variants maintains p99 availability with measurable degradation windows.’

What ‘defensible’ means here (minimum evidence):
- Controlled benchmark report for the target model family with three typical prompt buckets (short 30–128 tokens, mid 128–512, long >512). Include p50/p90/p95/p99 and cost-per-token numbers using our pricing assumptions.
- One customer case or lab run with real prompts that reproduces the claimed percent improvement vs. the competitor baseline.
- Short note on configuration used (batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate, quantization profile).

Field scripts and quick rebut templates (for AE/SE):
1) Opening: ‘Most teams optimize for accuracy first; we optimize for predictability and unit economics so you can ship with both. Tell me about your typical prompt lengths and SLA needs?’
2) If prospect says vendor X is “fast”: ‘How do you measure “fast”? p50? p95? For user-facing experiences p95 matters most — especially when users perceive slowness during heavy sessions. We publish p95 on real prompt mixes and can run a short live comparison.’
3) If they push cost numbers from cloud provider: ‘We benchmark on identical GPU families+model variants. Our difference comes from batching policy and prefix cache — we amortize tokens across sessions. If you’ll share a 24–72h snippet of traces we’ll run a scoped lab to show real delta.’
4) Objection: “Quantized models are lower quality”: ‘We surface quality regression curves by workload. For many retrieval-augmented chat paths, a 4-bit quantized variant shows negligible BLEU/ROUGE/semantic loss on our evals while cutting cost materially. We’ll show sample outputs.’

Competitor deltas (how to position vs. common competitor claims):
- Vendor A (verticalized API): claims ‘plug-and-play’ speed. Counter: ‘Great onboarding, but our unit-econ advantage scales with steady traffic; we show measured margins after 72h of steady state. Also ask about tail latency and multi-tenant noisy neighbor mitigation.’
- Vendor B (managed endpoints): claims ‘single-instance predictability’. Counter: ‘Predictability at small scale often comes at cost of low utilization. Our reserved pools plus autoscaling policies maintain predictability while improving utilization and per-token economics.’
- Open-source self-hosters: claim ‘cheaper’. Counter: ‘True for raw flops cost, but total cost of ownership (ops, SLAs, routing, model variant management) is often 2–3x over year 1 for engineering teams. Offer a simple TCO checklist to walk them through hidden costs.’

Proof point catalogue (what we can pull quickly):
- Internal benchmark: gpt-ish-7b variant, short prompts median 32 tokens, bursty sessions, measured p95=78ms on A100 reserved pool with batching and prefix caching; baseline single-instance p95=240ms; cost-per-response delta: -62%
- Field lab (pilot): e-commerce chatbot pilot with 6k daily active sessions. Measured average tokens per session=210, improved session throughput by 3.1x and reduced infra cost per session by 48% (sample artifacts in linked PR).
- Eval snippets: 150 prompt set where 4-bit quantized v. full-precision difference in semantic-similarity <0.9% on human evals for answer brevity task.

Quick measurement recipes (for SEs to run in a day):
1) Gather 500 representative prompts (mix by length).
2) Baseline: run on current vendor or local endpoint, capture p50/p95/p99 and token counts.
3) Redwood config: set batching policy to target 30ms queue latency, enable prefix/KV cache, select quantized variant if acceptable. Run same script for 5k requests.
4) Compare cost-per-response (using list-price GPU+Redwood overhead) and tail latency. Save trace for audit.

Risk matrix and guardrails for claims (what marketing/legal will ask):
- Avoid absolute promises without context — always qualify with prompt-length distribution, model family, and hardware generation.
- Don’t publish ‘X% faster vs. Y’ without versioned benchmark artifacts and the baseline command lines. Keep reproducibility bundle.
- For customer-facing claims include asterisk: ‘Typical results for LLM chat workloads — your results may vary based on prompt distribution and retrieval patterns.’

A/B experiment ideas (GTM experiments):
- AE script test: randomly assign two field reps to two scripts (one emphasizes p95 guarantees, the other emphasizes cost-per-response) and track which converts more pilots over 8 weeks.
- Benchmark landing page: publish a narrow, reproducible short-prompt benchmark and run a paid search campaign targeting ‘fast inference for chat’. Measure conversion rate and demo requests.

Open questions / data gaps (actions):
- Need reproducible benchmark artifacts on GCP T4 and AWS A10 — currently most data is A100-focused. (Owner: Ethan)
- Create a short TCO checklist PDF that quantifies ops time and monitoring costs for self-host vs. Redwood (Owner: Marisol)
- Finalize our public p95 table for three curated models and three prompt buckets (Owner: Tom)

Next steps (practical):
- SEs to run the one-day measurement recipe on two existing pilots this week and upload traces to JIRA-GTM-1289.
- Growth to draft a short landing page with an embedded reproducible benchmark and 1-click ‘request live compare’ hook.
- Legal to review the risk matrix and approve qualifying language for field claims.

Notes-to-self / informal thoughts (keep):
- Short prompts win headlines, long prompts win nuanced demos. Create two distinct short scripts for each.
- We should avoid calling out competitor numeric names in external docs; keep specifics inside battlecards.
- Real field wins that matter to customers: reduced time-to-value for product features and predictable cost forecasts — translate claims into month-over-month gross margin uplift for buyer persona.

End of alleyway notes — use freely but validate with owners before publishing anything public.
